title: BIDIRECTIONAL CHARGING FOR NEW BMW MODELS: E.ON AND THE BMW GROUP ARE EXPANDING THEIR VEHICLE-TO-GRID (V2G) OFFERING.
summary: The BMW Group and E.ON are expanding their joint Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) offering: in addition to the BMW iX3, drivers of the new BMW i3, BMW iX4 and BMW iX5 can now also opt for the V2G solution. With four models across different vehicle segments, all powered by the sixth-generation BMW eDrive techno
text:
The BMW Group and E.ON are expanding their joint Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) offering: in addition to the BMW iX3, drivers of the new BMW i3, BMW iX4 and BMW iX5 can now also opt for the V2G solution. With four models across different vehicle segments, all powered by the sixth-generation BMW eDrive technology (Gen6), the partners are making bidirectional charging accessible to a wider customer base.

Charging Neue Klasse bidirectional: Save up to 720 euros a year – and charge up to 16,000 km for free. *

The joint product package combines the bidirectional BMW Wallbox Professional with E.ON’s V2G electricity tariff, thereby intelligently integrating compatible BMW electric vehicles into the electricity grid. An algorithm developed by BMW and E.ON automatically controls both charging and the feeding of energy back from the high-voltage battery into the electricity grid. The intelligent control system takes the desired minimum state of charge into account, ensuring that customers’ individual mobility needs are met at all times.

For every hour that the vehicle is connected to the wallbox and V2G is activated, customers receive a 24 cent bonus, totalling up to 60 Euros per month. This means customers can receive up to 720 euros per year in connection bonuses. With the new BMW i3, this allows them to travel up to 16,000 kilometres free of charge. *

In addition, every kilowatt-hour fed back into the grid is compensated at 42 cents. Users can keep an eye on their charge level and bonus at any time via the My BMW app.

No impact on battery life: intelligent functions ensure that the high-voltage battery is always maintained at an optimal level to maximise its lifespan.

Scaling up the joint pioneering work at the interface between energy and mobility.

For all drivers of electric BMW and MINI vehicles: An alternative route into energy market integration. Cost-optimised charging has long been possible – not only through the V2G service, but also for all BMW and MINI electric vehicle drivers, including an attractive E.ON tariff with a charging bonus.

The BMW Group thus offers a solution for all customers who wish to charge their fully electric- or plug-in hybrid BMW or MINI intelligently whilst reducing home charging costs.

The vehicle is automatically charged at a selected location, taking into account the planned departure time and the desired state of charge, when electricity prices are particularly low.

The function is available for every electrified BMW and MINI model across all drive generations and can be used with the BMW/MINI Wallbox Plus, the Multifunction Charger (MFC) and any other charging product that charges using alternating current (AC).

Customers simply need a suitable electricity tariff that supports the BMW ‘Remote Charging Control’ function.

These tariffs are offered by many compatible electricity providers, such as E.ON. With this exclusive partner offer from E.ON, BMW and MINI customers in Germany can save up to €240** per year through smart charging and receive an additional €50*** bonus on top of the existing new customer bonus.

You will therefore benefit from the following advantages:

A significant reduction in home charging costs

Tailored to individual mobility needs

An additional E.ON bonus of 50 euros on top of the new customer bonus

* With the E.ON V2G electricity tariff, customers receive a bonus based solely on the time compatible BMW models are connected to the BMW Wallbox Professional, provided that Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) is activated as a use case, regardless of whether charging or discharging actually takes place. The bonus amounts to 24 cents per hour; with a maximum of 250 charging hours per month, this equates to 60 euros per month or 720 euros per year. Based on an average electricity price of 32.97 cents/kWh, the bonus covers up to 2,184 kWh charged per year.

Depending on the vehicle configuration of the BMW i3 50 xDrive, this covers, on a theoretical basis, an annual mileage of around 13,500 to 16,000 kilometres (WLTP), with a driving consumption of 13.5 to 16.1 kWh/100 km according to WLTP. In addition to the bonus, there is a feed-in tariff for every kilowatt-hour fed back into the grid.

** The €240 night-time charging bonus (granted until 31 December 2028) represents the maximum bonus amount you can receive per year by using the E.ON ÖkoStrom¹ Home & Drive 12, E.ON ÖkoStrom¹ Home & Drive 24 and E.ON ÖkoStrom¹ Home & Drive Connect 12 electricity tariffs. To receive the night-time charging bonus for the E.ON ÖkoStrom¹ Home & Drive electricity tariff on your annual statement or next regular bill, you must complete six charging sessions per month, with the vehicle connected for at least four hours between 00:00 and 06:00, have an active connection of your electric vehicle via CarConnect, and have a smart metering system (smart meter) installed or at least ordered. (1: Electricity equivalent to the amount you consume is generated from renewable energy sources located in Germany and fed into the power grid. Verification is provided through the cancellation of Guarantees of Origin with the German Environment Agency.)

*** One-time bonus for new customers. A new customer is anyone who was not an E.ON customer at the specified point of consumption during the six months prior to receipt of the order. The bonus will be credited on the first bill after the start of the contract. One-time additional bonus: The bonus will be credited on the first annual bill under this contract. The additional bonus will be added to the new customer bonus on invoices and will not be shown as a separate bonus in correspondence or on invoices. The bonus will no longer apply if the contract is terminated before the end of the initial contract term. If the customer is supplied by E.ON under the terms of this contract, the bonus will not be forfeited if the customer terminates the contractual relationship due to a price adjustment.

title: 2 HOURS 46 MINUTES OF CHARGING FOR 5,886.7 KM: FROM THE NORTH CAPE TO TARIFA IN THE NEW BMW i3 50 XDRIVE.
summary:
The challenge

After 1,007 km on a single battery charge, in the BMW iX3 50 xDrive from Debrecen to Munich: the BMW EfficientDynamics Team has taken on a new challenge.

The Paneuropeana – the benchmark for range and charging speed: Launched by Rafael de Mestre, it represents the ultimate test of ef
text:
The challenge

After 1,007 km on a single battery charge, in the BMW iX3 50 xDrive from Debrecen to Munich: the BMW EfficientDynamics Team has taken on a new challenge.

The Paneuropeana – the benchmark for range and charging speed: Launched by Rafael de Mestre, it represents the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed and, consequently, the long-distance capability of electric cars.

The key criterion of this extraordinary road trip: Who can travel across Europe via specified checkpoints with the shortest total charging time?

The route

The route begins at the North Cape, a headland jutting out into the Arctic Ocean on the northern side of the Norwegian island of Magerøya. It lies approximately 2,100 km south of the North Pole at 71° 10′ 21″ N / 25° 47′ 40″ E – and is thus the northernmost point of continental Europe accessible by car.

The route ends in Tarifa, situated at the easternmost end of Spain’s Costa de la Luz in the Andalusian province of Cádiz. At 36° 0' 23'' N / 5° 36' 31'' W – and thus the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

The stages and checkpoints have been deliberately chosen so that the focus is not on speed on the road. The vehicles taking part in the Paneuropeana are regular road users travelling along country roads, motorways and through towns.

However, the charging points are not pre-determined. And alongside a highly efficient vehicle with outstanding fast-charging capability, this is where the challenge lies: optimising the route between checkpoints specifically to make the best use of the charging infrastructure, whilst also taking into account external factors such as the weather, traffic jams, etc.

The Paneuropeana Performance

In numbers: On the Paneuropeana, the BMW i3 crossed eight countries, covering 5,886.7 km on motorways, country roads and through towns.

On average, it consumed just 12.5 kWh per 100 km. This figure is actually below the official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18–13.4 kWh/100 km. The driving time alone was 3 days, 2 hours and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h. The BMW i3 50 xDrive was charged en route exclusively at publicly accessible charging points within the respective national charging networks.

The BMW i3 50 xDrive, which was driven at all times by a single engineer in the vehicle, was accompanied by an identical BMW i3 and a BMW iX3 50 xDrive acting as support vehicles. All vehicles were 100 per cent identical in terms of hardware and software to the standard production specification available to customers.

Record: 2 hours, 45 minutes, 54 seconds of DC high-performance charging

The BMW i3 50 xDrive spent this time at the charging point whilst travelling through Europe, at an average charging power of 275 kW. The BMW i3 50 xDrive has thus set an impressive record, strikingly underlining the unrestricted long-distance capability of modern BMW electric models.

The car

For more than five decades, the BMW 3 Series has stood for unmistakable sporting driving pleasure, distinctive design and consistent technical progress. In 2026, the new BMW i3 – the first fully electric BMW 3 Series based on the Neue Klasse – will make its debut. It enhances the familiar character of the BMW 3 Series with new, outstanding features.

The new BMW i3 features the sixth generation of BMW eDrive technology. This comprises fundamentally new high-voltage batteries with cylindrical cells, highly efficient electric motors, 800-volt technology and bidirectional charging functionality. Compared with the previous generation, the BMW eDrive system – known as Gen6 – offers significantly greater ranges, improved efficiency and enables considerably faster charging.

The challenger: the new BMW i3 50 xDrive, with one electric motor on each of the front and rear axles. It has a total system output of 345 kW/469 PS and a maximum torque of 645 Nm. It accelerates from 0 to 100 km/h in 4.7 seconds. It features a 108.7 kWh high-voltage battery (usable energy) comprising lithium-ion cylindrical cells, which are integrated into the vehicle according to the ‘cell-to-pack’ and ‘pack-to-open-body’ principles. It achieves a maximum range of up to 912 km (WLTP). Its top speed is 200 km/h.

DC charging capacities of up to 400 kW also ensure drastically reduced charging times. At a DC fast charger, the BMW i3 50 xDrive can recharge enough energy for up to 423 km (WLTP) in 10 minutes.

BMW Efficient Dynamics @ Neue Klasse

Under the name BMW EfficientDynamics, an exceptional technology package was first introduced into series production at BMW in 2007. The promise to customers describes an apparent contradiction: more driving pleasure – lower fuel consumption. What was measured in litres of fuel for combustion-engine models, both then and now, is measured in kWh for all-electric models.

The outstanding EfficientDynamics features of the record-breaking BMW i3 50 xDrive:

a drag coefficient of just 0.21 – the most aerodynamically efficient BMW to date. The tyres have a rolling resistance that is 14 per cent better than the ‘A’ efficiency label stipulates. The wheels on the BMW i3 during its record-breaking run: 19-inch M Aerodynamic Polygon 1061 M wheels.

Energy losses in the Gen6 electric motors have been reduced by 40 per cent compared to the Gen5. The volumetric energy density of the Gen6 cylindrical cells has been increased by 20 per cent compared to the prismatic cells of the Gen5. The energy recuperation performance of the Gen6 has reached a new level: the high-performance computer ‘Heart of Joy’ controls more than 95 per cent of all braking processes via the electric motors – thereby feeding energy back into the high-voltage battery.

Made in Munich

The BMW i3 is manufactured at the BMW Group plant in Munich, the BMW Group’s original production site. For more than a hundred years, the plant in Milbertshofen, in the north of Munich, has been producing premium vehicles. Over the past four years, the plant has undergone extensive modernisation: in addition to a new body shop, a state-of-the-art vehicle assembly facility, including logistics areas, has been built.

summary: Milan. text:
Milan. BMW Motorrad once again chooses EICMA as the stage for the next phase of its growth strategy, built on expanding the motorcycling community, making motorcycling accessible to a new generation of riders and advancing the technological excellence that has always defined the brand. At the traditional international press conference, Sergio Solero, President and CEO of BMW Italia, and Markus Flasch, CEO of BMW Motorrad, outlined the brand’s vision, its achievements and the key new models making their debut in Milan.

At the heart of the presentation are three new motorcycles representing two ends of the BMW Motorrad spectrum: the new F 450 family, designed to make entry into the BMW world even more engaging and intuitive, and the new BMW M 1000 RS, an uncompromising expression of expertise developed in racing.

BMW F 450 R: a new expression of accessible riding

The new BMW F 450 R introduces an entirely new offering in the 48 hp sporty naked segment.

Lightweight, agile and intuitive, the F 450 R has been designed to deliver maximum riding pleasure for A2 licence holders, newcomers and returning riders. With a ready-to-ride weight of just 175 kg, a seat height of 790 mm and particularly accessible ergonomics, it is one of the most inclusive models ever developed by BMW Motorrad.

The new 420 cc parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree crankshaft configuration delivers 48 hp, combining exceptionally smooth operation with a distinctive sound. Standard equipment includes three riding modes, ABS Pro, Dynamic Traction Control, MSR, DBC, heated grips, full LED lighting and a 6.5-inch TFT display.

A key feature is the new Easy Ride Clutch, which further simplifies the riding experience and helps make the motorcycle accessible to an even wider audience.

BMW F 450 RR: entry into the world of RR

Making its debut alongside the naked model is the new BMW F 450 RR, a supersport motorcycle that brings the DNA of BMW Motorrad’s renowned RR models to the A2 segment.

With 48 hp, a ready-to-ride weight of just 177 kg and a chassis developed specifically for sporty riding, the F 450 RR offers a unique combination of lightness, precision and performance.

The new 420 cc parallel-twin engine with a 135-degree offset develops 43 Nm of torque and provides the technical foundation for a motorcycle featuring supersport geometry, a compact wheelbase, 17-inch wheels and performance-focused ergonomics.

Standard equipment includes Race mode, ABS Pro, DTC, DBC, MSR and a 6.5-inch TFT display, while the optional Riding Modes Pro package adds Race Pro mode and a lap timer for an experience even closer to riding on the track.

In terms of design, the new F 450 RR interprets the RR design language with a silhouette inspired by the S 1000 RR, aerodynamic winglets, asymmetrical fairings and a clearly race-oriented riding position.

With the debut of the F 450 RR, the new BMW F 450 family is now complete, comprising three distinct models: GS, R and RR.

BMW M 1000 RS: the world’s most powerful hyper naked makes its debut

The highlight of the evening was the world premiere of the new BMW M 1000 RS.

Drawing directly on the experience gained with the BMW M RR, the M 1000 RS brings genuine superbike technology to the hyper naked segment for the first time.

With a maximum output of 218 hp and a wet weight (without fuel) of just 185 kg, the new M 1000 RS achieves a power-to-weight ratio of approximately 1.18 hp/kg, positioning it as a contender for the title of the world’s most powerful hyper naked.

The RS designation, short for Rennsport, recalls some of the most iconic racing motorcycles in the brand’s history, including the RS 255 and RS 54, and introduces a new interpretation of BMW Motorrad performance.

An engine derived from the M RR, carbon winglets, a full titanium exhaust system, a brushed aluminium fuel tank and numerous carbon-fibre components define the new M 1000 RS, a motorcycle developed to deliver an intense riding experience, absolute precision and benchmark performance.

Three M limited editions and three motorcycles celebrating heritage and racing

Further enriching BMW Motorrad’s presence at EICMA 2026 are motorcycles that showcase the brand’s ability to combine innovation, exclusivity and a proud racing tradition.

Among them are the three exclusive BMW M Nürburgring Limited Edition models, commemorative editions inspired by the legendary German circuit and produced in limited numbers to honour the connection between BMW Motorrad and one of the world’s most iconic motorsport venues. These models embody the highest levels of technology, performance and distinctive design within the M range.

Displayed alongside them is the striking BMW K 18 Concept, unveiled at the Concorso d’Eleganza Villa d’Este. This visionary interpretation of touring combines imposing proportions, sculptural design and a contemporary reinterpretation of the renowned BMW boxer engine, demonstrating the brand’s ability to explore new forms of motorcycle design.

Completing the display is the FIM Endurance World Championship-winning BMW M 1000 RR (FIM EWC), a key contender in the championship-winning season and a symbol of technology transfer between racing and production models. The motorcycle demonstrates BMW Motorrad’s increasingly prominent role in international racing and the effectiveness of solutions developed on some of the world’s most demanding circuits.

These models complement the key new products presented at EICMA 2026, offering visitors a comprehensive view of the BMW Motorrad world: from the accessibility of the new F 450 family to the extreme performance of the M 1000 RS, encompassing design, heritage and success at the highest levels of racing.

A look ahead

BMW Motorrad’s presence at EICMA 2026 looks beyond the current product line-up to the brand’s future development. The exhibition provides an opportunity to preview some of the strategic directions that will shape the future range: a new generation of supersport models, the arrival of a new character within the GS family and the start of production of the forthcoming BMW R 20, derived from the concept that won acclaim from the public and critics at Villa d’Este. This evolution underlines BMW Motorrad’s commitment to continued innovation, expanding its offering while remaining true to the values that define its identity.

Good morning, Ladies and Gentlemen.

I’d like to begin with a few general remarks.

After the first nine months of the year, we achieved an operational performance of 3.5 percent EBIT-Margin in the Automotive Segment. Despite the difficult business environment, we reached Group earnings of 2 billion euros in Q3.

At the same time, we are driving the structural transformation of the company forward – across all levels. We are making good progress. And we want to take the opportunity this year to pick up the pace even further.

Therefore, we proactively decided to expand our portfolio and structural measures, to accelerate the necessary change. Accordingly, we adjusted our guidance for 2026.

I will hand over to Walter to run us through the Q3 figures and outline the financial impact of yesterday’s decision. After that, I will provide a strategic update.

PART II

Ladies and gentlemen,

At the end of September, we presented our strategic outlook at our Capital Market Day. We outlined where we stand and how we are positioning our company for the future.

We also confirmed our long-term target range of 8 to 10 percent EBIT margin in the Automotive Segment. We aim to achieve this target at the beginning of the next decade. And as you know, we have set an interim target of 3 to 5 percent EBIT margin in 2028.

To improve our profitability and to reach these targets, significant measures are needed. As we presented at the end of September, we are tackling all major business processes.

In sales, we are preparing the rollout of our direct sales model for the BMW brand in Europe, which will start next year. We are also taking measures to expand our offering at the high end of our product portfolio. We are therefore looking at introducing an additional offering above the current top-end model, the BMW X7, tailormade for the U.S. market.

In engineering, we want to reduce the development cycle significantly. At the same time, we are reviewing the number of variants across our entire portfolio and will reduce complexity.

In purchasing, we are reorienting our sourcing strategy and leveraging strategic partnerships, “Industry Best Offer” and

AI applications.

In parallel, we are streamlining our organizational structures across all divisions of the BMW AG to become more agile and efficient.

Today, I’d like to focus on our progress since the Capital Market Day regarding the transformation of our company and the successful rollout of the Neue Klasse. After that, I will give you an outlook on the months ahead.

Ladies and Gentlemen,

In the last few weeks, we have launched many initiatives across the whole company and we have already made significant progress. For example, we are accelerating the streamlining of our organizational structures, including the announced 20 percent reduction of the senior vice president roles.

As an important enabler of our transformation, we started a voluntary severance program. The program focused on all indirect employees of the BMW AG in Germany. Due to strong interest, we will be able to complete the program in a short amount of time. This highly positive response to the program opens up more significant potential to faster streamline our structures.

We have deliberately decided to take advantage of the opportunity this year to expand our wide set of structural measures to further accelerate the transformation. Based on this decision, we aim to finalize most of our company’s organizational transformation by the middle of next year. This will enable us to significantly improve our agility and the profitability of our organization.

In addition, we are rolling out the Neue Klasse products at remarkable pace across the portfolio and all powertrains. After the success of the BMW iX3*, many other models have followed, including the updated 7 Series, the 3 Series with BEV and ICE variants, the X5 with multiple drivetrain options, as well as the iX4*.

Neue Klasse production is up and running in Debrecen, Munich, Dingolfing, Spartanburg and Shenyang. In Debrecen, we have already expanded operations to three shifts to meet demand. There, the iX4 will be produced alongside the iX3.

We will further enhance our leading position in the BEV premium segment.

All BEV variants of the Neue Klasse are powered by our new sixth-generation high-voltage batteries. At the beginning of October, we opened our new Plant in Irlbach-Straßkirchen, which will supply our German plants. Just three weeks ago, I joined the opening of our Gen6 facility in Shenyang. Series production in Woodruff, South Carolina will begin before the end of this year, with San Luis Potosí, Mexico following next year.

In line with this growing production capacity and demand, we have significantly increased the ramp-up of the Gen6 models this year. This will allow us to phase out some Gen5 BEVs sooner than planned, with an additional impact on 2026 earnings. Looking ahead, the better margins of the Gen6 products will help drive the transformation of our portfolio and increase profitability.

The speed up of our structural transformation and the fast ramp-up of the Gen6 technology – both reflect our confidence in our path forward.

This brings me to our priorities for the next months.

With our global market strategy, we are increasing our

regional set-up to tailor our offering to the different needs

of the markets.

In Europe this means strengthening our presence in the

high-volume entry premium segment by introducing another fully electric BMW model in 2028.

In the U.S. we continue to deliver on the strong customer demand for SAVs with our plant in Spartanburg that is running at full capacity.

China remains a key focus for us.

The rollout of the Neue Klasse begins this month with the market launch of the iX3 in China. Feedback from the pre-drives of the new iX3 and i3 has been extremely positive. In particular, our ADAS with the unique BMW Symbiotic Driving has been very highly rated.

Going forward, we will further strengthen the local R&D and sourcing functions to be even more focused on Chinese customer needs and to address them at a faster pace.

We are also looking to leverage our production network in Shenyang more broadly by considering exports of vehicles manufactured in China to markets in Asia Pacific.

All in all, we are taking steps in all of our major regions to develop our local footprints further and to localize our supply chains. This is the basis for a more resilient and profitable global set up.

Ladies and eGentlemen,

As mentioned, we are committed to our long-term profitability targets. For this, we are driving the transformation of our processes and structures forward and, with the Neue Klasse, we are rolling out an extensive product portfolio.

We are seeing high demand for Neue Klasse models, and we have made very positive progress with the workforce restructuring program. Therefore, we have now actively decided to expand the portfolio and structural measures, while focusing on the successful rollout of the Neue Klasse.

By doing this we are laying the foundation – starting next year,

for reaching our next milestone in 2028, and therefore staying

firmly on course towards our long-term ambitions.

Thank you.

SLIDE 2: BMW Group Quarterly Statement to 30 September 2026

Ladies and Gentlemen,

Good morning.

The BMW Group continued to operate in a challenging global market environment in the third quarter, with significant differences across regions.

Volume growth in Europe and the US partially offset the decline in China and Asia-Pacific.

In this environment, we remain focused on the factors that we can directly influence, with continued discipline on costs and operational performance.

Against this backdrop, our third-quarter financial performance was in line with expectations.

SLIDE 3: BMW Group Performance in Q3 and YTD September 2026

Let me start with an overview of our Group performance in the third quarter.

Group revenues amounted to more than 30 billion euros in the quarter and almost 93 billion euros after nine months.

Our diversified business model once again supported our Group result.

Group earnings before tax totalled 2.1 billion euros in Q3, benefiting from both our Financial Services business and the positive development of interest rate derivatives.

After nine months, Group EBT amounted to 6.1 billion euros.

Accordingly, the Group EBT margin stood at 6.8 percent in the third quarter and

6.6 percent year-to-date.

In the Automotive Segment, EBIT amounted to 901 million euros in the third quarter, corresponding to a reported EBIT margin of 3.4 percent.

The margin benefited from the settlement reached with our supplier in connection with the IBS brake system warranty case.

At the same time, the margin also included two familiar items:

First, elevated tariffs had an impact of around 1.25 percentage points.

And second, depreciation from the BBA purchase price allocation reduced the margin by 1.2 percentage points.

The expenses related to our workforce restructuring program will be recognized in the P&L in the fourth quarter. They will impact the full-year EBIT margin by around 1.25 percentage points.

After nine months, Automotive EBIT amounted to around 2.9 billion euros, with an EBIT margin of 3.5 percent.

SLIDE 4: Automotive Retail Units, BEV Units and Auto Revenue

Let me now provide more detail on the performance of the Automotive Segment.

In the third quarter, the BMW Group delivered around 551,000 BMW, MINI and Rolls-Royce vehicles to customers, 6.3 percent less than in the same quarter last year.

Automotive Segment revenues declined by 6.5 percent to 26.7 billion euros, largely reflecting lower vehicle deliveries and the continued competitive intensity in several markets.

While overall deliveries and revenues were below the prior-year level, our BEV retail sales gained further momentum in the third quarter, as demand remained strong across key markets.

With over 110,000 deliveries, an increase of 7.2 percent year-on-year, our all-electric models accounted for one in five units sold worldwide.

Including plug-in hybrids, sales of electrified vehicles amounted to more than 150,000 units, which corresponds to an electrified vehicle share of 27.4 percent.

SLIDE 5: BMW Group Regional Sales – Growth in Europe and the US partially offset declines in China and APAC

Let’s now take a closer look at our sales performance across the major regions.

In Europe, our largest sales region, retail sales increased by 2.6 percent year-on-year.

Europe also remains the main BEV growth driver. Here more than one in three vehicles sold were all-electric.

Including plug-in hybrids, the European electrification ratio came close to

50 percent.

In the US, retail sales grew by 2.5 percent in the third quarter and 3.5 percent after nine months, outperforming a declining overall market.

In China, weak consumer demand continued to weigh on large parts of the automotive market, particularly in the non-electrified vehicle segment.

In this environment, BMW Group retail sales declined by 24.8 percent in the third quarter. This was in line with the overall market, which was down 24.6 percent.

We continue to focus on balancing volumes, pricing and profitability in this highly competitive market.

At the same time, we are preparing for the market launch of the long-wheelbase BMW iX3* in November, followed by further Neue Klasse models throughout 2027.

In our sales region Asia-Pacific, Eastern Europe, Middle East, and Africa, retail sales declined by around 8,000 units, or 10.9 percent year-on-year.

Several markets in the region were affected by weaker consumer sentiment resulting from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, as well as increasing competitive pressure linked to spillover effects from China.

Let’s now take a closer look at the year-on-year development of Automotive EBIT on the following slide.

SLIDE 6: Automotive Segment EBIT in Q3 2026

Changes in currencies reduced EBIT by around 100 million euros year-over-year, while raw material positions were broadly neutral.

As expected, the year-over-year currency headwind was significantly lower in Q3 than in the first two quarters of the year.

The net effect of volume, model mix and pricing had a negative impact of around 600 million euros compared to the third quarter of 2025.

This mainly reflects lower volumes in China and continued pricing pressure in several markets.

Total Group R&D expenditure remained below the prior-year level at 1.8 billion euros, decreasing by 6.8 percent year-on-year.

Research and development expenses recognized in the P&L, however, increased by around 200 million euros, mainly due to higher depreciation on capitalized development costs from previous years.

The R&D ratio according to the German Commercial Code came in at 5.9 percent for both the third quarter and the first nine months.

We continue to make progress in reducing our operating cost base. As a result, selling and administrative expenses decreased by around 100 million euros year-on-year in the third quarter.

Other Cost Changes had a positive EBIT impact of 400 million euros, mainly reflecting the settlement reached with our supplier in connection with the IBS brake system warranty case.

As a result, Automotive EBIT amounted to 901 million euros in the third quarter and 2.9 billion euros after nine months.

SLIDE 7: Automotive Segment Free Cash Flow in Q3 2026

Let’s switch to Free cashflow in the Automotive Segment, starting with earnings before tax of around 900 million euros.

The net change in working capital contributed around 600 million euros, mainly reflecting lower inventories as we have adjusted production schedules in line with market demand.

The net effect of capital expenditure and depreciation contributed positively by around 600 million euros, as depreciation continued to exceed capital expenditure.

We expect depreciation to remain above capital expenditure for the full year 2026 and beyond.

The capex ratio was 3.9 percent for the first nine months.

The change in provisions reduced free cashflow by around 900 million euros in Q3, mainly reflecting the consumption of provisions for warranties and bonus payments.

Other items reduced free cashflow by 1.8 billion euros.

This mainly reflects timing effects, as some of the accruals that supported free cashflow in the second quarter reversed in the third quarter.

In total, Automotive Free cashflow amounted to minus 566 million euros in the third quarter.

After nine months, it stood at 724 million euros.

As you know, the BMW Group is steering Automotive free cashflow on an annual basis.

For the full year, we continue to target more than 2.5 billion euros of Automotive free cashflow.

In the fourth quarter, we expect significant positive cash contributions from further working capital reduction and tariff refunds.

Ladies and Gentlemen,

the BMW Group remains committed to its shareholder return strategy, combining attractive dividend payments with share buybacks.

The third and final tranche of our current third share buyback program is expected to be completed in November.

With this, we will have completed the entire 2-billion-euro program five months ahead of the original schedule.

This reflects our disciplined approach to capital allocation and our focus on creating value for our shareholders.

Under the current program, we will have returned around 1.25 billion euros to shareholders through share buybacks in 2026.

News on share buyback program four will follow in due course. As stated at our Capital Market Day at the end of September, we are currently reviewing our shareholder return framework.

SLIDE 8: Financial Services Segment YTD September 2026

In our Financial Services Segment, new business remained at a high level.

During the first nine months, we concluded around 1.3 million new contracts with retail customers, a slight increase of 1.3 percent year-on-year.

Adjusted for FX effects, total new business volume grew by 3.3 percent to around 49.4 billion euros.

At the same time, the penetration rate for lease and loan products increased to

53.7 percent.

This development was supported by a more favourable competitive environment in China since mid-2025.

Our Financial Services balance sheet volume reached 159 billion euros at the end of September.

This represents an increase of more than 5 percent year-on-year, driven by retail financing and leasing contracts.

Quarterly earnings were stable year-on-year, with segment EBT amounting to

639 million euros.

For the first nine months, segment earnings totalled 1.65 billion euros, down 10.3 percent year-on-year.

This decline results from an addition to an existing provision in the first quarter, which was related to a consumer compensation program in the UK.

Overall, the segment continued to grow and made an important contribution to Group earnings.

The credit loss ratio across the entire credit portfolio increased to 0.35 percent at the end of September.

This reflects the sale of non-performing loans in the third quarter.

SLIDE 9: Motorcycles Segment in Q3 2026

In the Motorcycles Segment, deliveries declined by 12.5 percent year-on-year to 46,600 units.

Segment EBIT for the third quarter totalled 33 million euros,

resulting in an EBIT margin of 4.8 percent.

SLIDE 10: Outlook 2026

Ladies and Gentlemen,

Building on our solid Q3 results that I just outlined, we took the decision yesterday to expand and intensify our portfolio and structural measures in the financial year 2026.

As we successfully ramp up the Neue Klasse, we will gradually phase out previous vehicle and technology generations earlier.

In addition, we are further accelerating the organizational realignment of the company.

Considering these measures, we have changed our outlook for the financial year 2026 for the following KPIs:

In the Automotive Segment, we now expect the EBIT margin to come in within a range of minus 0.5 percent to (plus) 0.5 percent.

I would like to reiterate that this full-year Auto EBIT margin includes our portfolio and structural measures.

Their impact on the margin was originally expected to be 1.25 percentage points.

After our decision to expand these measures, we now anticipate a total burden of around 2.5 percentage points.

That means that – without these measures – the Auto EBIT margin is still expected to be above 2 percent.

Accordingly, the Return on Capital Employed (RoCE) in the Automotive segment is expected in a corridor between minus 1 percent and (plus) 1 percent.

Given the changes to our 2026 outlook, we will consider the impact of our portfolio and structural measures when determining the level of shareholder returns for the 2026 financial year.

SLIDE 11: Based on solid Q3 results, BMW Group expands and intensifies measures.

Ladies and Gentlemen,

Our diversified global business model enables us to manage diverging developments across regions and support the overall performance of the Group.

On this basis, the BMW Group achieved earnings before tax of more than 6 billion euros in the first nine months of 2026.

For the full year 2026, we continue to expect an Automotive EBIT Margin above

2 percent before portfolio and structural measures and an Automotive Free Cashflow of more than 2.5 billion euros.

At the same time, we are seeing positive momentum from the initiatives we launched in 2026.

We are now moving into the next phase of our transformation: rolling out the technologies of the Neue Klasse across our portfolio, simplifying structures and processes, and further reducing complexity across the company.

Artificial intelligence will play an increasingly important role in driving these changes.

Going forward, we will further reduce operational costs as well as R&D and capital expenditure to improve our long-term profitability.

For the full year 2026, we expect both R&D and capex to be below prior-year levels.

In 2027, we will be heading back towards our strategic corridors, which are

4 to 5 percent for R&D and less than 5 percent for capex.

As outlined at our Capital Market Day, we are targeting an Automotive EBIT margin of 3 to 5 percent in 2028 and aim to return to our strategic target range of 8 to 10 percent by the beginning of the next decade.

The decision that we took yesterday is an important step towards achieving these targets.

On that basis, we will create sustained value for all our stakeholders.

Thank you.

summary: The BMW Group is decisively and rapidly aligning for the future: at the backdrop of a solid third quarter, the Board of Management of the Munich premium manufacturer has therefore decided to further expand and intensify portfolio and structural measures. text:
The BMW Group is decisively and rapidly aligning for the future: at the backdrop of a solid third quarter, the Board of Management of the Munich premium manufacturer has therefore decided to further expand and intensify portfolio and structural measures. While the Group result in the third quarter proved robust at more than €2 billion and was only moderately below the prior year (Q3: €2,083 million / -10.6%; YTD Q3: €6,128 million / -23.9%), the measures now decided will lead to a non-operational earnings impact in the Automotive segment in the fourth quarter.

As of September, the BMW Group was also successful in maintaining course to meet its full-year financial targets in this highly competitive environment, as demonstrated by the EBT margin of 6.8 % for the quarter (YTD Q3: 6.6%) and the EBIT margin in the Automotive segment of 3.4 % (YTD Q3: 3.5%) – giving the company the financial scope to expand its measures.

While the Automotive segment’s operative EBIT margin before consideration of restructuring measures continues to be expected above 2.0% for the full year, the BMW Group has adjusted its outlook for the reported figure and now expects a full-year EBIT margin between -0.5% and +0.5% (previously: 1–3%). The company’s stable operational performance is underlined by its expectations for Free Cash Flow in the Automotive segment: for 2026 it maintains the expectation that the Automotive Free Cash Flow will be above €2.5 billion.

Portfolio measures are driven by the sustained strong demand for Neue Klasse models, to which the BMW Group has responded by introducing additional production shifts at an early stage. The resulting acceleration of the production ramp-up creates an opportunity to begin phasing out previous vehicle and technology generations earlier, including selected models based on Gen5 battery technology.

The Neue Klasse, including its technology clusters such as Gen6 technology, is set to become a major driver of profitability improvement over the coming years, supported by its high level of innovation and enhanced cost efficiency.

The technology is already available in models such as the BMW iX3*, BMW i3*, BMW i7*, BMW iX4* and BMW iX5*, and will be rolled out to many more models in the coming months.

At the same time, the company intends to leverage the momentum generated by its workforce restructuring program to expand its organizational and process realignment. For example, the reduction in management functions will be implemented faster than announced.

“Current developments in our industry call for decisiveness and swift implementation. We will therefore specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures,” said Milan Nedeljković, Chairman of the Board of Management of BMW AG, on Wednesday in Munich. “By doing so we are realigning our company and improving our agility and long-term competitiveness. This lays the foundation for unlocking the full potential of our unique technology and product portfolio with the Neue Klasse in the coming years.”

The global market launch of the Neue Klasse has advanced further in recent months: its highly innovative models and technologies serve as the catalyst for the next phase of realignment and will contribute to the BMW Group’s long-term profitable growth.

As presented at the Capital Markets Day at the end of September, it also plans further measures to boost profitability and competitiveness: the Group will build on its consistent premium and multi-brand strategy as well as technology openness, while enhancing regionalisation of product range and expanding the high-end segment.

The BMW Group is also increasing the focus on value creation – to this end, the company will expand the use of high-quality “Industry Best Offer” solutions, which optimally combine innovation, scalability and cost-efficiency whilst securing efficiencies in development, procurement and production.

By leveraging the use of artificial intelligence, the company aims to focus even more on agility and impact. Agentic AI is increasingly becoming a productive part of day-to-day business. Whether used in crafting bespoke customer offers or as a digital colleague in procurement planning, AI agents pool knowledge, automate process steps and lay the foundations for faster and more informed decisions.

“Speed is a key success factor in our planned realignment. That is why we are intensifying measures to enhance efficiency and streamline structures already this year. In doing so, we intend to strengthen our future margins and be on course to deliver our profitability targets,” said Chief Financial Officer Walter Mertl.

Growth in the US and Europe, lower sales in China

In the third quarter, the BMW Group delivered 551,075 vehicles to customers – down (-)6.3% compared with the prior-year quarter. In total, the BMW Group recorded 1,707,802 deliveries over the nine-month period (-4.9%). Growth in Europe (in Q3: +2.6%; YTD Q3: +4.5%) and the US (in Q3: +2.5%; YTD Q3: +3.4%) could only partially offset the ongoing headwinds in the Chinese market.

Fully electric vehicles accounted for one-fifth of the BMW Group’s total sales in the third quarter (BEV + PHEV: 27.4%). In the Europe sales region, almost half of the vehicles delivered were electrified (46.9%; BEV share: 34.7%).

In China, the market environment remained challenging overall in the third quarter. BMW Group sales were down by a quarter compared with the previous year, which fell in line with the decline of the total market. The company is preparing for the market launch of the iX3 LWB in November, as well as further models from the Neue Klasse during 2027.

In the third quarter, the BMW Group posted revenues of €30,452 million (-5.8%; adjusted for currency translation effects -7.7%; YTD Q3: -7.3%; adjusted for currency translation effects -6.6%).

Moderate decline in R&D spending and capital expenditure

Since the peak in 2024, the company has seen a gradual decline in R&D expenditure and plans to meet the defined target ranges. Research and development expenditure fell moderately in the third quarter to €1,790 million and €5,504 million over the nine-month period respectively (Q3: -6.8%;

YTD Q3: -7.4%). As in the previous year, the research and development ratio stood at 5.9% – both as in the third quarter and YTD September.

Capital expenditure fell significantly over the nine-month period to €3,657 million (-17.1 %; Q3: €1,757 million / +4.6%). The capex ratio as YTD September stood at 3.9% (2025: 4.4%; Q3 5,8%; Q3 2025: 5.2%). A capex ratio of less than 6% is also forecast for the full year.

Group EBT margin of 6.8% in third quarter

Group earnings before tax (EBT) of €2,083 million in the third quarter and €6,128 million after nine months (Q3: -10.6%; YTD Q3: -23.9%) benefited from positive valuation effects on interest-rate derivatives, particularly in the first and third quarters. The Group EBT margin was 6.8% in the third quarter and stood at 6.6% as of YTD September (Q3: -0.4 percentage points; Q3 YTD: -1.5 percentage points).

In the three-month period, the Automotive Segment generated revenues of €26,669 million (in Q3: -6.5 %; adjusted for currency translation effects -8.5 %; YTD Q3: -7.1 %; adjusted for currency translation effects -6.5 %). Lower manufacturing costs reduced the cost of sales. Lower sales volumes and strong competition in the global automotive sector, particularly in China, dampened the segment’s revenue performance. This was compounded by negative currency effects.

Segment earnings before financial result (EBIT) for the third quarter totalled €901 million (-39.7%; YTD Q3: -43.8%). The settlement of the legal proceedings relating to the Integrated Braking System had a positive impact.

The EBIT margin came in at 3.4% for the third quarter (-1.8 percentage points; 2026: 3.5%; 2025: -2.4 percentage points). In Q3 and the year to date, operating performance was impacted by 1.2 percentage points, owing to the well-known depreciation and amortisation of BBA assets resulting from the purchase price allocation, and, additionally, expenses related to higher import tariffs amounting to around 1.25 percentage points – after around 1.75 percentage points in previous year’s quarter respectively 1.5 percentage points in the first nine months of 2025.

Free cash flow of automative segment expected at >€ 2.5 billion in full-year

The Automotive Segment’s free cash flow for the first nine months totalled

€724 million. In the third quarter, free cash flow amounted to - €566 million (2025: €2,688 million; Q3 2025: €343 million). The company maintains the expectation that the segment free cash flow will be above €2.5 billion.

Stable operating performance in Financial Services Segment

In the Financial Services Segment, the number of new financing and leasing contracts concluded increased slightly in the first nine months of 2026 to 1,292,663 contracts (+1.3%; in Q3: -5.4%).

For the third quarter, the segment reported profit before taxes (PBT) of

€639 million in the third quarter and €1,647 million for the year to the end of September (Q3: -0.8%; YTD 2026: -10.3%). A significant headwind resulted from the addition to an existing provision in connection with the industry-wide compensation scheme for car financing customers in the United Kingdom made in the first quarter of 2026.

Guidance for 2026 adjusted

The expenses associated with the expansion and intensification of portfolio and structural measures described above will weigh on BMW Group’s operating result in the fourth quarter.

Therefore, the company now expects an Automotive segment EBIT margin in the corridor of -0.5% to +0.5%; the EBIT margin before portfolio and structural measures continues to be exptected above 2.0%. Car deliveries are expected to be moderately below the prior year.

The Automotive segment RoCE is expected to be in a range of -1% to +1%.

Return on Equity (RoE) in the Financial Services segment is forecast at 13–16%.

In the Motorcycles segment, deliveries are now expected to be slightly below last year’s level (previously: on par with last year’s level). The EBIT margin is expected to be in a range of 4.0–6.0%, and RoCE in a range of 10–14%.

The full-year guidance includes adverse effects on the EBIT margin in the Automotive segment of approximately 1.25 percentage points from increased tariffs, 1.2 percentage points from depreciation and amortization of BBA assets resulting from purchase price allocation, and approximately 2.5 percentage points from portfolio and structural measures.

The BMW Group’s actual business performance may deviate from the expectations outlined above – for example, due to changes in political and macroeconomic conditions.

Deliveries to customers

A new or used vehicle is recorded as a delivery once it is handed over to the end user (which also includes leaseholders under lease contracts with BMW Financial Services). In the US and Canada, end users also include (1) dealers when they designate a vehicle as a service loaner or demonstrator vehicle and (2) dealers and other third parties when they purchase a company vehicle at auction and dealers when they purchase company vehicles directly from the BMW Group. Deliveries may be made by BMW AG, one of its international subsidiaries, a BMW Group retail outlet, or independent third-party dealers. The vast majority of deliveries – and hence the reporting of deliveries to the BMW Group – is made by independent third-party dealers. Retail vehicle deliveries during a given reporting period do not correlate directly to the revenues that the BMW Group recognises in respect of that particular reporting period.

title: BMW GROUP UPDATES GUIDANCE FOR THE 2026 FINANCIAL YEAR
summary: The Board of Management of BMW AG updated today the full year guidance for the 2026 financial year. This follows the Board’s decision to expand and intensify portfolio and structural measures. While operating financial performance remained solid in the third quarter, the measures approved will resul
text:
The Board of Management of BMW AG updated today the full year guidance for the 2026 financial year. This follows the Board’s decision to expand and intensify portfolio and structural measures. While operating financial performance remained solid in the third quarter, the measures approved will result in a non-operating impact on earnings in the Automotive segment in the fourth quarter.

The following financial KPIs in the outlook for the 2026 financial year were changed as outlined here:

EBIT Margin Segment Automotive: in the corridor -0.5% to +0.5% (before: in the corridor of 1-3%); the EBIT margin before structural and portfolio measures continues to be expected above 2.0%.

RoCE Segment Automotive: in the corridor -1% to +1% (before: in the corridor of 1-5%).

The company’s stable operating performance is underscored by the unchanged expectation for Free Cashflow in the Automotive segment: The BMW Group maintains the expectation that the Automotive Free Cashflow will be above €2.5 billion in 2026.

Furthermore, the Board of Management of BMW AG changed the following KPIs in the full year guidance as outlined here:

Deliveries in Segment Automotive: moderate decrease versus previous year (before: slight decrease).

Share of all-electric cars in deliveries in Segment Automobile: slight increase versus previous year (before: at previous year’s level).

CO2e emissions scope 3 supply chain and use phase in Segment Automobile: slight decrease versus previous year (before: at previous year’s level).

Deliveries in Segment Motorcycles: slight decrease versus previous year (before: at previous year’s level).

The portfolio measures stem from the sustained high demand for Neue Klasse models, to which the BMW Group has responded by introducing additional production shifts at an early stage. The resulting acceleration of the production ramp-up creates an opportunity to begin phasing out previous vehicle and technology generations earlier, including selected models based on Gen5 battery technology.

With its technology clusters, such as Gen6 technology, the Neue Klasse will contribute to improving the company’s profitability in the coming years by its high level of innovation and enhanced cost efficiency.

At the same time, the company intends to leverage the momentum generated by its workforce restructuring program to expand its organizational and process realignment more quickly and comprehensively. For example, the reduction in management functions will be implemented faster than announced.

Details are provided in the Q3 Report, which will be published on 4th November 2026. The definitions of the KPIs can be found in the Glossary of the BMW Group Report 2025 on pages 429 to 431.

title: BMW GROUP STARTS PRODUCTION OF THE NEW BMW 3 SERIES AT PLANT DINGOLFING
summary: This week, the BMW Group began series production of the eighth generation of the BMW 3 Series at Plant Dingolfing. The site manufactures the new BMW 3 Series Sedan with combustion engines (and, in future, also with plug-in hybrid powertrains). The model adopts the design language and integrates key
text:
This week, the BMW Group began series production of the eighth generation of the BMW 3 Series at Plant Dingolfing. The site manufactures the new BMW 3 Series Sedan with combustion engines (and, in future, also with plug-in hybrid powertrains). The model adopts the design language and integrates key technologies of the Neue Klasse, including BMW Panoramic iDrive, a new electrical and electronic architecture, and new driver assistance systems.

Clear allocation of production between Munich and Dingolfing

The BMW Group is allocating production of the new BMW 3 Series generation to two German vehicle plants: BMW Group Plant Munich produces the all-electric BMW i3. BMW Group Plant Dingolfing manufactures the BMW 3 Series Sedan variants with combustion engines and, from 2027 (see above), plug-in hybrid powertrains.

This allocation reflects the BMW Group’s technology-open approach and enables it to accommodate different customer requirements and powertrain concepts. In total, around one billion euros has been invested in the further development of the Munich and Dingolfing vehicle plants for this purpose.

In Dingolfing, the new BMW 3 Series Sedan is produced flexibly alongside BMW 4 Series and BMW 5 Series models on a shared production line in assembly hall 50. The production equipment can accommodate different powertrain variants.

Key components for the new BMW 3 Series Sedan come from BMW Group Plant Landshut, the largest component manufacturing site in the BMW Group’s production network. The site supplies, among other items, crankcases and cylinder heads for four- and six-cylinder engines, as well as the propeller shaft, a key component in power transmission.

Landshut also manufactures interior components such as the instrument panel, including the glove compartment. In the cockpit, newly developed lighting technology adds a distinctive touch to the interior of the new BMW 3 Series Sedan: an integrated light box backlights a variety of surface materials. At BMW Group Plant Landshut, this innovation progressed from pre-development through industrialisation to series production

With its high level of vertical integration and broad technology portfolio, Plant Landshut makes a significant contribution to the value of the new model generation.

An iconic model returns

The first generation of the BMW 3 Series, the BMW E21, was already being manufactured in Dingolfing from 1980. Several generations of the BMW 3 Series Sedan were produced there until 2004. From 2013 to 2021, the plant also manufactured the BMW 3 Series Gran Turismo. In total, more than 1.15 million BMW 3 Series vehicles have rolled off the production line in Dingolfing to date. The BMW 3 Series has been one of the BMW brand’s core models for more than 50 years. Since its market launch in 1975, around 18 million vehicles in the series have been sold worldwide.

Efficient integration into existing production structures

The new BMW 3 Series Sedan was integrated into existing production structures quickly, flexibly and efficiently. In the paint shop and assembly, the BMW 3 Series can largely be manufactured on existing lines using proven modular processes. Adaptations were primarily required for Neue Klasse innovations, such as BMW Panoramic iDrive and the associated changes to cockpit pre-assembly.

In the body shop, a new powertrain-neutral production line was installed within the existing building. The plant takes a systematic approach to reuse: around one third of the approximately 750 robots, as well as other equipment components, come from existing production facilities. Modern technologies, such as automatic best-fit adjustment of doors and closures and automated surface inspection, provide additional support for quality assurance.

Inbound logistics has also been further automated and digitalised. Automated forklifts, Splitbots and around 250 Smart Transport Robots work together intelligently to support incoming goods deliveries and the supply of materials to production.

These measures are part of the ongoing development of BMW Group production in line with the BMW iFACTORY vision. This combines lean production with resource conservation and digitalisation. Automation, artificial intelligence, intelligent robotics and digitalised logistics processes support efficiency and quality.

Investments strengthen the Dingolfing site

BMW Group Plant Dingolfing is the BMW Group’s largest European production site. Around 18,000 employees and approximately 950 apprentices work at the site. The plant produces around 1,350 vehicles per day. In addition to the new BMW 3 Series, its model range includes BMW 4 Series, BMW 5 Series and BMW 7 Series models, as well as the BMW iX, vehicles from BMW M GmbH and the BMW 7 Series Protection.

Outlook

The start of production marks the beginning of the series production ramp-up for the eighth generation of the BMW 3 Series at BMW Group Plant Dingolfing. The market launch will take place in stages from the first quarter of 2027. By the end of 2027, the BMW Group plans to bring around 40 new or updated models featuring Neue Klasse technologies onto the road.

title: THE WORLD´S MOST POWERFUL HYPER NAKED BIKE.
summary: With the new BMW M 1000 RS, BMW Motorrad presents the world’s most powerful hyper naked bike – powered by the superbike engine from the BMW M 1000 RR and delivering its full output of 218 hp. text:
With the new BMW M 1000 RS, BMW Motorrad presents the world’s most powerful hyper naked bike – powered by the superbike engine from the BMW M 1000 RR and delivering its full output of 218 hp. In doing so, the M 1000 RS pushes the boundaries of the hyper naked segment. 218 hp meets a wet weight of just 185 kg (without fuel), superbike technology meets an upright, direct riding position, and radical performance meets an unmistakably deep, dark aesthetic. Limited to 1,000 units, the M 1000 RS is an exclusive statement for riders who do not want to explain maximum performance, but to experience it.

Radical presence. Ultimate performance.

The BMW M 1000 RS consistently transfers the high-performance credentials of the BMW M 1000 RR to the hyper naked segment. Its character is radical and immediately apparent: powerful, precise and uncompromising. No fairing distracts from its technology, and no detail is an end in itself. The M 1000 RS makes its capabilities visible – with a deep, dark aesthetic, powerful proportions and the self-assured stance of a motorcycle that fears no comparison.

218 hp. An unequivocal claim to leadership.

At its heart is the superbike engine from the BMW M 1000 RR, which delivers its full output of 218 hp in the BMW M 1000 RS. As a hyper naked bike, it therefore pushes the boundaries of its segment. Combined with a wet weight of just 185 kg, this results in an exceptional power-to-weight ratio – and immediate performance that is present in every riding situation. The BMW M 1000 RS combines explosive acceleration, precise control and the agility of a hyper naked bike with the technological rigour of a superbike.

High-tech. Down to the last detail.

The technical basis is the BMW M 1000 R with the M Competition Package. The M rider footrest system from the BMW M 1000 RR and a seat height increased by 20 mm create a riding position that is significantly more front-wheel oriented than on the BMW M 1000 R, underlining the uncompromisingly sporty character of the M 1000 RS. Building on this foundation, the concept is sharpened consistently: an M full titanium exhaust system underscores its lightweight-construction and performance credentials. Matt carbon M winglets with RS lettering combine a distinctive racing look with aerodynamic function. The rear end of the BMW M 1000 RR makes the transfer of technology from the superbike segment clearly visible. Matt carbon components, the brushed aluminium fuel tank, new graphics and the M seat in Alcantara look with RS embroidery define its exclusive, dark presence.

Racing. Redefined.

The RS designation has a special history at BMW Motorrad. Models such as the BMW RS 255 Kompressor of 1935 to 1939 and the later BMW RS 54 stand for racing at the highest technological level. The BMW M 1000 RS takes this tradition into a new dimension: an uncompromising hyper naked bike with the heart of a superbike and the ambition to own the fast lane.

1,000 units. Maximum exclusivity.

The BMW M 1000 RS is limited to 1,000 units worldwide and will be available from BMW Motorrad dealers from March 2027. The retail price in Germany is €40,000, including 19 per cent VAT.
